newsitem.title: LEBANON: Blast kills two Israeli-allied militia in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Blast kills two Israeli-allied militia in Lebanon.

text.p: Two Israeli-backed militiamen were killed and two badly wounded when a roadside bomb set off by Hizbollah guerrillas exploded near their patrol in south Lebanon on Friday, security sources said.
They said the bomb exploded as the South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia patrol passed in the Jarmaq area in the early morning in the central sector of a border zone Israel occupies in south Lebanon.

Two SLA men were immediately killed and two seriously wounded in the incident -- bringing to 16 the number of militiamen killed in south Lebanon this year. The Moslem guerrillas have also killed 21 Israeli soldiers in 1996.
In Beirut, a Hizbollah (Party of God) spokesman claimed responsibility for the attack.
The pro-Iranian Hizbollah militant fighters are waging a guerrilla war to oust Israeli troops from the 15-km (nine-mile) -wide occupation zone in south Lebanon.

In April, Israel launched an air, sea, and naval bombardment against Lebanon spurred by the guerrillas rocketing northern Israel. Some 200 Lebanese, mostly civilians, were killed in the onslaught. No Israelis were killed.
That fighting ended with a U.S.-brokered ceasefire forbidding the sides to fire from or on civilian areas.
